Homage to the Illustrious Great Lord of the Gaṇas. May there be auspiciousness; may there be no obstacles.
We worship the elephant-faced one, the sun to the lotus of the unborn, who possesses many tusks for his devotees, yet is single-tusked himself, day and night.
The root mantra of Vighneśvara.
May there be auspiciousness; [herein is] the root mantra of Vighneśvara. (l.1)

To the elephant-faced one, to the long-bellied one, to the remnant-eater, to Gaṇeśa, to the Self—Oṃ Klau Kviṃ Gaṇeśā Ve Ve, to the bestower of the fruits of all desires, Svāhā! Oṃ, to the elephant-faced one... [to the thumbs], homage! To the long-bellied one, to the index fingers, homage! To the remnant-eater, to the middle fingers, homage! To the Self who is Vināyaka, to the ring fingers, homage! To the Self who is Ekadanta, to the little fingers, homage!

Salutation to the self whose ears are like winnowing baskets with both palms and backs of the hands. Salutation to the elephant-faced one at the heart. Svāhā to the pot-bellied one at the head. Vauṣaṭ to Ucchiṣṭa at the tuft of hair (śikhā). Huṃ to Vināyaka at the armor (kavaca). Vaiṣaṭ to the single-tusked one at the three eyes. Haṃ to the self whose ears are like winnowing baskets at the weapon (astra); thus is the binding of the directions (digbandha). The visualization (dhyāna): [One should meditate on] the five [faces], restless upon the mouths of women and young girls, deluded by passion.

[The recitation] with one's own [consort] seated on the lap... the *liṅga*, the grandson, the root mantra, the recitation, the conclusion, as before? It is complete. *ka e ī la hrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *ha ka ha la hrīṃ śirase svāhā*. *saka la hrīṃ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ*. *saka la hrīṃ kavacāya huṃ*. *hasaka ha la hrīṃ kavacāya huṃ*. *hasaka la hrīṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*. *sakalakastūrikāṃ hrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*. *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om*—thus is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*). The visualization (*dhyāna*):
[She who] possesses musk that kisses her forehead, [and is] smeared with saffron.
One should meditate upon Ambikā during the rite of recitation— she who possesses a gentle smile and a glance, who holds a bow, arrows, a noose, and a goad;
she who deludes all people, who is adorned with garlands and garments of compassion,
and who is radiant like a hibiscus flower.

Having worshipped with *laṃ* and all the offerings beginning with earth (*pṛthivī*), one should recite the root mantra: *a e ī su hrīṃ hasakaharabhaṇīṃ sakalasya hrīṃ sakalahrīṃ hasakalya hrīṃ sakalyahrīṃ mūlam*. Then, having performed the visualization (*dhyāna*) regarding the hands, body, nose, and so forth, one should worship with the five offerings beginning with earth using *laṃ*, saying: "Obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī."
